items.title: Serenoa repens for benign prostatic hyperplasia.
items.journal: The Cochrane database of systematic reviews
items.summary: Cochrane systematic review found Serenoa repens (saw palmetto) extract showed no significant improvement in urinary symptoms or flow measures compared to placebo for BPH.

items.title: Saw palmetto for benign prostatic hyperplasia.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.summary: Large randomized controlled trial of 225 men found saw palmetto extract (160 mg twice daily) showed no benefit over placebo for moderate-to-severe BPH symptoms over one year.

items.title: Current Treatment for Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia.
items.summary: Comprehensive review of current BPH treatments including pharmacological options like alpha-blockers, 5-alpha reductase inhibitors, and surgical approaches.

items.title: Medical Treatment of Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia.
items.journal: The Urologic clinics of North America
items.summary: Review of primary medical treatments for BPH-associated LUTS covering alpha-1 antagonists, anticholinergics, PDE5 inhibitors, 5-alpha reductase inhibitors, and beta-3 agonists.

items.title: Minimally Invasive Treatment in Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH).
items.summary: Systematic review of minimally invasive treatments for BPH including PAE, TUNA, TUMT, HIFU, laser treatments and cryoablation as alternatives to surgery.

items.title: Efficacy and Safety of Xialiqi for the Treatment of Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia in a Randomized Trial.
items.summary: Randomized controlled trial of 395 patients found Xialiqi capsules (traditional Chinese medicine) showed efficacy for moderate BPH-related LUTS over 8 weeks.

items.title: Efficacy evaluation of Chinese herbal medicine, VGH-BPH1, for patients with benign prostatic hyperplasia: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, and crossover study.
items.journal: Journal of the Chinese Medical Association : JCMA
items.summary: Crossover randomized controlled trial found Chinese herbal medicine prescription VGH-BPH1 failed to show significant benefit as add-on treatment for BPH symptoms.

items.title: Serenoa repens extract for benign prostate hyperplasia: a randomized controlled trial.
items.summary: Double-blind placebo-controlled trial of 100 men found 320 mg Serenoa repens extract showed no significant difference from placebo in IPSS scores or peak urinary flow rate.

items.title: Effectiveness of the addition of tadalafil to tamsulosin in the treatment of acute urinary retention in patients with benign prostatic hyperplasia: A randomized clinical trial.
items.summary: Randomized clinical trial of 80 patients found adding tadalafil to tamsulosin showed no additional benefit for treating acute urinary retention in BPH patients.

items.title: The rising worldwide impact of benign prostatic hyperplasia.
items.summary: Global Burden of Disease analysis showing the rising worldwide impact of LUTS attributed to BPH from 1990 to 2017.

canonicalFacts.claim: BPH is characterized by disorders of urine storage and bladder emptying, affecting most men over age 60 to some degree
Transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP) has long been considered the gold standard for operative BPH treatment
Medical management typically starts with tamsulosin and progresses to combination therapy based on patient response
Minimally invasive treatments like PAE, TUNA, TUMT, HIFU, and laser treatments are valid alternatives to surgery for BPH
